text.p: Shareholders of Duracell International Inc on Monday voted to approve a merger with Gillette Company. Duracell's board of director unanimously approved the merger on September 12.
The merger was approved by 99.44 percent of the shareholders present at the meeting.
Duracell Chairman and Chief Executive Charles Perrin told Reuters after the meeting that the merger would help broaden Duracell's international business.

"Gillette is in a lot of the developing world, where Duracell isn't, so we can combine the Duracell sales force and the Gillette sales force in the developing markets of Latin America, Asia Pacific and Africa," he said. "That should be a really good combination and help the Duracell brand grow globally."
Perrin said that about 70 percent of Gillette's business was outside the United States, compared to 55 percent of Duracell's business.
"Gillette is focused technologically and they invest a lot in R&D, so they should bring some more financial resources to Duracell." He did not elaborate.
The merger will be effective by the end of Tuesday, December 31.
